newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices slide with crude selloff.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices slide with crude selloff.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly lost ground Tuesday in sluggish activity, with slack utility demand and a tumbling crude market pressuring most grades, industry sources said.

"There is oil around and demand is not great, and with crude coming off, it will be hard to raise prices now," said one cash trader. But he said rising demand into Florida could eventually help stabilize the complex.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent slipped a quarter to about $15.00 a barrel, with May one percent paper down more than 25 cents to sub-$15 on weaker crude, traders said.
While firm gas prices also could help by encouraging some fuel switching to resid, traders said fading spring demand would temper any rush to buy.
High sulphurs in New York also were about a quarter lower, with 2.2 percent now pegged at $14.25-50, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour was unchanged at $16.25.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices also lost ground, with one percent 25 cents lower at $14.75-15.00 and three percent down a similar amount to $13.25.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate swing gas prices were unchanged Tuesday at about $2.35/mmBtu, or $14.81 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed slightly to about $2.10/mmBtu, or $13.23 a barrel.
